title: The growth tick's 180s foreground timeout SIGKILLs ContentGenerator mid-render, abandoning paid-for renders
evidence: The 13:08 EDT tick ran growth:sync_cadence in the foreground with a 180s budget; a 5-render shortfall takes ~45 min end-to-end (each render ~6 min: torch.compile init + 35/25-step inpaint + NSFW gate + realism gate + Ollama caption + schedule), so the tool call was killed mid-render. Result on 2026-09-19: PipelineRun 471 (sync_producer=Growth::ContentGenerator, created 17:01:15Z) had its render complete (job 7555 -> completed 17:04:53Z, ImageCandidate created) but the process that could write the terminal status was gone; the run sat pending until ReconcileStaleRuns reaped it at 18:38Z. The same failure produced the 42 pending runs cleaned up by hand earlier today and the tick's own report flagged it: 'a fixed 180s foreground timeout will repeatedly kill it mid-render'. Cost is real GPU time spent for renders that may never reach a scheduled post.

notes.note: Damage is now BOUNDED in-repo: ReconcileStaleRuns (2026-09-19) terminalises abandoned sync runs at 30 min so they stop tripping the stuck-run probe. That fixes the debris, not the waste -- the producer still dies mid-render. The remaining fix is in the cron prompt, which is Hermes config outside this repo: tc-growth-harness-brain must not run growth:sync_cadence under a fixed 180s foreground budget. Options, cheapest first: (1) run it detached (direct >> log 2>&1 &) and let the next tick's render_need top up what is missing -- sync_cadence counts existing posts, so a partial run is safe to resume; (2) split it into per-slot batches (one render per call, ~10 min budget); (3) raise the tick's tool timeout above the observed ~45 min worst case. Filed rather than acted on because the prompt lives in ~/.hermes/profiles/turbo-carnival/cron/jobs.json, outside this repo.

FIXED repo-side (commit c7d298a): Growth::RenderSalvage recovers renders a killed producer abandoned instead of losing them. For a sync-produced run untouched past a 30-min grace with an active candidate whose file exists and no Photo row for that path, it re-runs BOTH gates, imports the photo, captions and schedules it; CadenceEngine runs it first, bounded by the outstanding shortfall, so the harness now prefers finishing an abandoned render over paying for a new one. Photo-by-path is the idempotency marker (re-runs recover nothing), one candidate per run, non-sync runs untouched, failures rescued so recovery can never break the sync. VERIFIED: 8 new specs green; live run against the production DB inside a rolled-back transaction selected exactly the 3 stranded candidates (runs 457/463/471 -> candidates 3180/3183/3184), re-ran the real gates, created photo 348 + post 341 (strategy_name=render-salvage, scheduled 2026-09-20T19:56Z) and left zero production writes after rollback. The SIGKILL itself is unchanged and tracked separately in growth-tick-launch-mode (Hermes cron config, needs Tim).
